panels.description: Evening on the pit rim. Alex draws a worn photograph halfway from his jacket; Grandmother smiles in it while Adrian’s face is folded and creased. Alex’s other hand is clenched in his pocket. Ada notices both. Keep the photograph and fist unobstructed; reserve three separated lettering pockets: Ada upper-left, Alex middle-left, Alex lower-right.

Ada faces Alex rather than the view as Oasis brightens and Keel dims. Keep the photograph visible between them. Reserve the upper-left for Ada’s question and upper-right for Alex’s answer, with open basin space carrying the silence.
Ada’s steady face fills the panel while Alex’s clenched hand occupies the foreground. Reserve the upper-left for her question and lower-right for his answer.

Alex and Ada stand small against the darkening basin and begin walking home at dusk. Alex stares toward the horizon; Ada lingers and looks back toward Oasis. Keep the bottom caption band clear and place Ada’s final small balloon near her without covering either figure.

items.speaker: ALEX
items.text: Some days she knows me. Other days she calls me Adrian...

items.speaker: ALEX
items.text: The hardest part isn't that she forgets. It's that she makes up crazy stories about him.

items.speaker: ALEX
items.text: That he wasn't wasting it. That he was working.

items.speaker: ADA
items.text: What do you actually remember about him?

items.speaker: ADA
items.text: So everything else is what people told you. What if they were wrong?

items.speaker: ALEX
items.text: Maybe… Or maybe they're right. Either way... he's gone.
